title: Sunny and the Flying Fox
author: Jamie Wigg
structure: p1 front cover, p2 title, p3-22 twenty story pages, p23 The End, p24 back cover
back_cover_blurb: As the sky turns the colour of ripe plums, little Sunny the quokka watches the flying foxes lift from the old fig tree and glide, soft and silent, across the evening. A calm, gentle bedtime tale for winding down and drifting off to sleep. Perfect for little ones ages 1-5.

pages.scene: the little quokka sits in a dim evening meadow of soft grasses and wildflowers, ears up, wide awake and curious, as the last daylight fades; gentle honey glow low on the horizon, first faint stars
pages.text: The day grew soft and the light grew low. Sunny the quokka was not sleepy — not quite yet.

pages.scene: wide dusk sky above the meadow turning deep plum and rose, the little quokka gazing up, a few dark shapes just beginning to rise far away over an old fig tree
pages.text: The sky turned the colour of ripe, sweet plums. And something began to move against it.

pages.scene: several flying foxes (fruit bats) lifting from the silhouette of a big old fig tree, wide dark wings spread, the little quokka watching from the grass below
pages.text: Flying foxes, sailing out from the old fig tree. One. Then three. Then many.

pages.scene: flying foxes gliding across the plum-navy sky with wide still wings, the little quokka standing very still in the meadow looking up in wonder
pages.text: Their wings were wide and dark, moving through the air without a single sound.

pages.scene: a flying fox in a long smooth glide across the twilight sky, stars appearing, the little quokka's face lit softly, watching
pages.text: No flap, no flutter — just a long, smooth, swooping glide. Sunny stood very still and watched.

pages.scene: the little quokka small in a big soft meadow beneath an enormous quiet sky full of gliding flying foxes, sense of gentle awe
pages.text: They were so large, and so very quiet. She had not known something so big could move so softly.

pages.scene: one flying fox swooping low and close over the meadow, warm dark fur and a small gentle fox-like face, the little quokka looking up close
pages.text: One flew low — close enough to see the warm dark fur and its little fox-like face.

pages.scene: close view of a gentle flying fox with neat ears, bright eyes and a pointed nose, hovering near a moonlit flowering tree, the quokka watching
pages.text: Neat little ears. Bright, kind eyes. A soft pointed nose.

pages.scene: a flying fox hovering at a pale moonlit blossom on a flowering tree, sipping nectar, soft glow, the little quokka watching from below
pages.text: It reached a pale moonlit blossom and drank, so gently, from the flower.

pages.scene: the flying fox lifting away and rising back up into the darkening starry sky, the little quokka following it with her eyes
pages.text: Then up it lifted, away again, back into the deep and darkening sky.

pages.scene: many flying foxes crossing the night sky along different long curved arcs, stars and a crescent moon, the meadow below soft and dim
pages.text: The others followed their own quiet paths — long curved arcs, each one different.

pages.scene: a mother flying fox gliding with a tiny baby flying fox clinging to her fur, tender, the little quokka watching warmly from the grass
pages.text: One carried a little one, tucked close and safe, clinging softly to her fur.

pages.scene: the whole evening sky gentle and full of soft dark wings gliding home, warm and peaceful, the little quokka small and content below
pages.text: The whole wide sky was soft with wings, all sailing gently home.

pages.scene: glowing fireflies drifting through the meadow grass around the little quokka, warm golden sparks, calm night settling
pages.text: Down in the grass, the fireflies woke and blinked their tiny golden lights.

pages.scene: the pale round moon climbing higher over the quiet meadow, cool silver light, the little quokka gazing up sleepily
pages.text: The moon climbed higher, pale and round, and hushed the meadow soft and still.

pages.scene: the little quokka giving a small sleepy yawn in the moonlit grass, eyes half closed, cosy
pages.text: And Sunny gave a small, slow yawn. The watching had made her sleepy at last.

pages.scene: the last flying foxes settling back into the distant old fig tree to roost, folding their wings, the little quokka watching from afar
pages.text: The flying foxes drifted home, to fold their wings and rest.

pages.scene: the little quokka padding home through cool silvery moonlit grass, sleepy and calm, stars above
pages.text: So Sunny turned for home, through the cool and quiet grass.

pages.scene: the little quokka curling into a soft cosy nest of leaves and grass, snug and warm under the stars, eyes closing
pages.text: She curled into the softest nest of leaves, warm and safe and snug.

pages.scene: the little quokka fast asleep and peaceful in her nest, a gentle smile, moon and stars glowing softly above, one flying fox gliding far away
pages.text: Her eyes fell closed. Above her, the soft wings sailed on through her dreams.

the_end_text:
The End.
Sweet dreams, little one. Goodnight.
